evidence: Live n=444 complete cases. Just-identified single-factor loadings from the live correlations (r12=0.5629, r13=0.5128, r23=0.4716) are satis_1 0.782, satis_2 0.719, satis_3 0.655, reproducing the rank order of the paper's Table 2 loadings SATIS1 0.91 > SATIS2 0.88 > SATIS3 0.64, with satis_3 lowest in both (0.655 vs published 0.64). This is the content prediction: Table 1's third bullet, 'Normally, this kind of experience makes me feel satisfied', is trait-level rather than trip-specific and must be the weakest indicator, while bullet 1 'Overall, I am satisfied with the experience' is the global item. Two further content predictions hold: bullet 2 ('met my vacation needs VERY WELL', the most demanding claim) has the lowest mean, 5.570 vs 6.023 and 5.838, and bullet 3 (a generic disposition statement) has the smallest SD, 0.974 vs 1.160 and 1.229. Absolute loadings differ from published because the paper estimated them inside the full 6-factor robust CFA; rank order is the signal. DOES NOT ESTABLISH: satis_1 vs satis_2 is separated only by a small gap (0.782 vs 0.719 observed, 0.91 vs 0.88 published) in the same direction, so the pairing of the first two bullets is consistent rather than pinned; only satis_3 is distinguished firmly. Item codes are a mechanical lowercase rename of the S1 File XLSX headers 'SATIS 1'..'SATIS 3', so code-to-column is not at issue; only bullet-to-number is.
